title: When the Wolf Wakes
premise: Sebastian Kavanagh, an exiled storm-caller living under a false name in the magic-hating city of Corvane, discovers the border wards fell the same night the stars went out—both casualties of a parasite called the Hollow Crown that has consumed King Aldric and now feeds on the kingdom's magic. Hunted by the crown's inquisitors, she allies with Warden Ilsa Vane, the woman who exiled her twelve years ago and who now carries proof of the king's corruption. To unbind Aldric, Sebastian must reclaim the storm magic she swore off, knowing the ritual will demand either her power or her life, while Ilsa must choose between loyalty to a dying crown and the truth that could shatter the realm. In the end, Sebastian pours her storm into the king to burn the Crown out, surviving only as an ordinary woman—and choosing to stay in Corvane, finally visible, finally belonging.
about_author: Astrid Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing storm records along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes fantasies about outsiders, broken oaths, and the weather that follows them.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Sebastian Kavanagh, selling charms under the name 'Seb the Tinker,' feels her suppressed magic stir when every star in the sky vanishes at once. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: dread beneath a carefully ordinary life—the first crack in twelve years of hiding.

chapters.title: Charms and Cinders
chapters.summary: In Corvane's market, Sebastian notices her small charms working too well, and a child's fever breaks at her touch. An inquisitor's clerk takes note of her stall. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: fear that her invisibility is ending, and a reluctant ache of wanting to help.

chapters.title: The Warden at the Door
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vane—the warden who exiled Sebastian twelve years ago—arrives wounded at her door, carrying the fallen border-ward sigil and a royal seal that bleeds shadow. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: guilt and old love colliding as she asks the woman she ruined for help.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Ilsa explains the wards didn't fail—they were eaten. The Hollow Crown, a parasitic intelligence bound to the royal line, has consumed King Aldric and is drinking the kingdom's magic dry. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: fury that her exile was tied to a lie Ilsa helped protect.

chapters.title: The King's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: The pair infiltrate a royal procession and see Aldric up close: alive, articulate, and utterly hollow, his shadow moving a half-second behind him. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: horror, and the first flicker of pity for the man behind the crown.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Hale
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Hale, who once spared Sebastian as a girl, corners her in the undercity—but he is half-consumed himself, begging her to end him before the Crown speaks through his mouth. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: grief and the cost of mercy.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Rain
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Sebastian's first uncontrolled storm killed her village's harvest and Ilsa, then her mentor, chose exile over execution to save her. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: the wound beneath their estrangement—Ilsa's loyalty was always a form of love.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: In a ruined star-temple, Ilsa's archived texts reveal the only way to free Aldric: a storm-caller must pour their full magic through the Crown, burning it out—at the likely cost of the caller's power, perhaps their life. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: terror and a grim, steadying resolve.

chapters.title: The City That Hates Magic
chapters.summary: Corvane's council, fed Crown propaganda, declares Sebastian the cause of the darkened sky; mobs burn the tinker quarter, and her neighbors—people she quietly protected for years—shelter her in their cellars. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: belonging arriving at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: A Crown's Bargain
chapters.summary: The Hollow Crown speaks to Sebastian through a dream, offering her exile's end, her magic legitimized, and Ilsa's safety if she walks away. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: temptation, and the discovery that the Crown fears her specifically.

chapters.title: The Warden's Oath
chapters.summary: Ilsa confesses to her own order that she hid the truth of Aldric's condition for a year; she is stripped of rank and marked for arrest. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: liberation in ruin—loyalty to a crown finally broken in favor of truth.

chapters.title: The Road to the Star-Temple
chapters.summary: Hunted across the frost plains, Sebastian and Ilsa argue about the rite's cost; Sebastian secretly plans to go alone so Ilsa won't have to watch her die. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened into a lie of protection.

chapters.title: What the Stars Remember
chapters.summary: In the star-temple's vault, the last living star-priest shows Sebastian that the Crown was once a guardian spirit, corrupted by the first king's greed—meaning it can be grieved, not just destroyed. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: compassion complicating her purpose.

chapters.title: Hale's Last March
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Hale, fully consumed, leads the Crown's hunters to the temple; Ilsa holds the pass alone and is gravely wounded buying Sebastian time. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: sacrifice as atonement, and the fear of dying unreconciled.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the King
chapters.summary: Aldric, briefly surfacing through the Crown's grip, sends a hidden message: he remembers his daughter, and asks only that someone tell her he fought. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the human stakes crystallize—this is a rescue, not just a battle.

chapters.title: Storm-Bound
chapters.summary: Sebastian unbinds her own sealing-oaths, and twelve years of caged storm erupts through her; she nearly destroys the temple before the priest's teachings anchor her. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: exhilaration and grief for the self she buried.

chapters.title: The Long Dark of Corvane
chapters.summary: With the wards gone and the Crown starving, the capital goes dark and cold; Ilsa, recovering, organizes the city's outcasts—witches, tinkers, exiles—into a defense that shouldn't work but does. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: the unloved finding each other.

chapters.title: The Throne Room
chapters.summary: Sebastian walks into the palace under a parley flag and confronts the Crown directly; it shows her every life her childhood storm touched, trying to drown her in guilt before the rite. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the darkest hour—guilt as a weapon turned inward.

chapters.title: When the Wolf Wakes
chapters.summary: Ilsa arrives bloodied to break the Crown's hold, and instead of letting Sebastian go alone, binds herself into the rite as anchor; the storm rises, and the Crown screams with the voices of every king it ate. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: love against duty, chosen openly at last.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: The climax: Sebastian pours her storm through Aldric while Ilsa holds the anchor-line; the Crown is burned out, the stars relight one by one, and Sebastian's magic gutters to nothing—she survives, but ordinary. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: triumph laced with loss.

chapters.title: The King Who Fought
chapters.summary: Aldric, freed and frail, abdicates in favor of a regency council; Sebastian keeps her promise and tells his daughter the truth of his fight, and Ilsa is offered her rank back and refuses it. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: quiet reckonings, debts honored.

chapters.title: A Shop with a New Sign
chapters.summary: Spring returns to Corvane; Sebastian opens a charm shop under her true name, magic slowly legalizing, with no storm inside her and no need for one. Ilsa stays, unranked and unrepentant. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted—home at last.
